findings.title: hostId is threaded to only one of the artifactContentUrl callers
findings.body: The new optional `hostId` is passed only from `ArtifactActionsMenu.tsx:254`. The other callers still resolve preview URLs against the local `getApiBaseUrl()`: `ArtifactPreviewModal.tsx:137`, `ArtifactThumbnail.tsx:53`, `FileMediaPreview.tsx:32` and `useSessionWorkspaceFiles.ts:362`. I read `ArtifactPreviewModal.tsx` and `FileMediaPreview.tsx`, and both already have a `hostId` in scope (`artifact.hostId` and the `hostId` prop). The PR body says "Artifact previews from connected remote hosts now use the correct host connection", which is only true for the issue-upload read. A remote-host `ao-preview-artifact.*.localhost` rawUrl in those other views still points at the local daemon. Either pass `hostId` there, or narrow the claim and say that is out of scope. I did not read `ArtifactThumbnail.tsx` or `useSessionWorkspaceFiles.ts` to check whether `hostId` is available there.

findings.title: Parentheses are stripped from the uploaded name silently and without a comment
findings.body: `input.name.replace(/[()]/g, "")` changes the filename GitHub receives, so `plan (1).md` becomes `plan 1.md`. The dialog still shows the original name (`GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:95`), and nothing explains why the characters are removed. Two different files, `a(1).md` and `a1.md`, end up with the same name. Add a comment giving the reason (presumably GitHub rejects parentheses in artifact names) so a later edit does not drop it. Consider showing the sanitized name in the dialog.

findings.title: Only one of the two refactored fallbacks is tested
findings.body: `bridge.ts:41-42` now points both `findArtifactIssues` and `publishIssueArtifact` at the shared `desktopIssueArtifactRequired`. The new test checks only `findArtifactIssues`. Add a `publishIssueArtifact` assertion so the existing rejection behaviour stays pinned.

findings.title: Browser fallback for findArtifactIssues now rejects instead of returning an empty list
findings.body: Before this change, `findArtifactIssues` in the browser-preview bridge resolved to `[]`. It now rejects with "Open the desktop app to add an issue artifact.". That is a deliberate improvement, since the dialog can show the reason, but it changes the contract of a fallback that other tests or e2e fakes may rely on. `frontend/e2e/support/fake-bridge.ts:96` still returns `[]`. I did not read how `GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx` renders a rejected search, so I can't confirm the message reaches the user.
